approval_boundary: Proposed settings. The user must approve this exact committed file hash and the exact batched run list before manual dispatch. An approval ID records that approval; it does not create it.

contract.vector_scope: D28 synthetic-only scan control; no inference, ANN execution or int8 recommendation

tier100.label: derived-100-repository fixture: 10 real source parts plus 90 correlated derived top-ups
tier100.review: Upload the manifest before timing. Lead review follows the run; a rejected manifest invalidates only tier100 results.

disk_admission: Free-space floors on RUNNER_TEMP before candidate timing, not measured peak bounds. Retain workspace and RUNNER_TEMP df logs after every execution phase. A capacity refusal blocks timing, never records a format miss, deletes no evidence and changes no cap or venue automatically. The base post-freeze formula is an additional admission floor.
software_cleanup: Base/linkdelta only: on a disposable github-hosted Linux VM, remove exactly /usr/share/dotnet, /usr/local/lib/android, /opt/ghc and /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL. Preserve all workspace, RUNNER_TEMP, job evidence, Go/Python/Node tools and other tool-cache entries. Plan roughly 30 GiB free immediately after cleanup, before later caches and fixtures: an unverified 14 GiB starting-space assumption plus a historical 16.7 GiB Android/.NET reclaim. GHC/CodeQL savings are not credited. Actual image occupancy varies; df and the unchanged timing floors decide admission.

basis./venue/cpus: study/storage/checks/base/README.md Estimate and limits, study/storage/checks/vector/README.md Sizing estimates, and study/storage/checks/fixtures/FIXTURES.md name a four-vCPU Ubuntu host.
basis./venue/job_memory_bytes: Integration proposal: 12 GiB enclosing cap on the reports nominal 16-GB host, above the 10 GiB tier100 target cap with two GiB inside the job for controllers and cache. Delegation and outside-owner cleanup follow .github/workflows/storage-screen.yml. This is not engine RSS or a measured requirement.
basis./venue/host_reserve_bytes: Integration proposal: require at least 2 GiB physical memory outside the enclosing cap for the runner and cleanup owner. The reports name a nominal 16-GB host; actual MemTotal is checked.
basis./venue/price_cap_usd: Zero-cost public-fork standard Linux CI venue only. No paid runner, model inference, cloud job or extra service is requested.
basis./venue/max_parallel: Approved D12 sets start at most three independent measurement jobs: Check 2 + plain Check 1 + Check 4, or one Check 5 tier per job. Every singleton starts one job. Vector/Check 6 is not selectable. All same-host A/B/C controls remain within one selected job.
basis./jobs/tests/timeout_minutes: Integration estimate: 45 minutes for setup, three readonly Go module vet/test pairs and three stdlib Python suites (base, fixtures and shared workflow helpers). This is not a measurement bound.
basis./jobs/base/timeout_minutes: Selected steps retain the conservative 350-minute envelope: fetch 10 + tiny generation reserve 5 + tier100 generation reserve 20 + setup 25 + main 209 + side reserve 60 + cleanup/upload 20 = 349 minutes. Tiny generation runs only for check2; tier100 generation runs only for check5-tier100. Check2 restores four tiny full correctness protocols inside main, not inside timed checks. No timeout increase is needed. F=max(60,ceil(9*P/67108864)) finalization seconds and the 30-second join come out of main/absolute first-step work, before the unchanged minute-329.5 wrapper cutoff. All bounds are unmeasured planning limits.
basis./jobs/base/setup_seconds: Integration reserve: 25 minutes for Go setup, downloads, serial builds, metadata and manifest freezing outside timing; unmeasured. The fixed unused-software removal shares this setup reserve; budget roughly 1-3 minutes, not a measured bound.
basis./jobs/base/cleanup_upload_seconds: Twenty minutes for owned-root cleanup and both freeze/result uploads. Driver finalization and its 30-second runner join come from the main envelope, not this upload reserve. The unchanged wrapper is a backstop at the absolute cutoff plus 30 seconds; unmeasured.
basis./jobs/linkdelta/timeout_minutes: C-LD-8 revised projection: (2*9000 serial tier deadlines + 600 fetch + 1200 setup + 1200 finalization/cleanup/upload) / 60 = 350 minutes. Timing phases have 330 minutes through setup/fetch, leaving 20 minutes inside this job for finalization and uploads. The job cap is 10 minutes below GitHub 360; that external margin is not extra usable runtime. Reserves and throughput are unmeasured, not guaranteed finish times.
basis./jobs/linkdelta/setup_seconds: checks-link-delta proposal relayed by lead: build/cleanup about 20 minutes. This envelope reserves 20 minutes for setup/build separately; unmeasured. The fixed unused-software removal shares this setup reserve; budget roughly 1-3 minutes, not a measured bound.
basis./jobs/linkdelta/cleanup_upload_seconds: Integration reserve: 20 additional minutes for cleanup, two-tier evidence and upload; unmeasured.
basis./jobs/vector/timeout_minutes: Hard job envelope: (600 setup + 600 generation + 600 measurement + 600 cleanup/upload) / 60 = 40 minutes.
basis./jobs/vector/setup_seconds: Integration reserve: 10 minutes for Go setup, serial builds, metadata and freeze, outside query timing; unmeasured.
basis./jobs/vector/cleanup_upload_seconds: Integration reserve: 10 minutes for owned-root cleanup and evidence upload; unmeasured.

basis./base/main_wall_seconds: Selected jobs retain a 12540-second main envelope minus the 30-second join and F=max(60,ceil(9*P/67108864)) finalization reserve. Check2 runs tiny full lifecycle correctness once for A, B, plain C and side C. Check1 runs three rotating A/B/selected-C rounds at tier1 and tier10; each Check5 job runs three rounds at only its named tier. Bytes runs one untimed tier1 build per variant. No timed step reruns tiny correctness; Check5 reduction requires the saved matching Check2 receipt. P is the actual protected-file byte total. The 64 MiB/s hash-rate assumption and timing envelope are unmeasured, not completion guarantees.
basis./base/side_wall_seconds: The unchanged 3600-second side reserve remains for the legacy combined regression path. Selected check1-side is its own approved job, using the main/absolute job deadline. Check2 checks both C variants before selection. No selected job adds a conditional side phase or changes samples, trials, queries or tiers.
basis./base/runs: Three rotating fresh-process rounds per selected timed tier, not warm passes in one process. Check2 instead runs one full tiny protocol for each of A, B, plain C and side C; bytes runs one untimed build per variant. Repeated hit/read sampling and the existing judged strata remain unchanged. Serving directories from timed/build-only runs are removed only after inventory receipts; failed outputs and full tiny lifecycle evidence are retained.
basis./base/safety_timeout_seconds: study/storage/checks/base/README.md proposed config sets the accepted runner safety timeout to 900 seconds.

basis./linkdelta/wall_seconds: C-LD-8 revised wall estimate from checks-link-delta: 9000 seconds per serial tier, unmeasured and conditional on planning rates of 100000 reference edge rows/s, 50000 reference node rows/s and 8000000 stored vector-coordinate JSON decodes/s. Across 144 workload sequences per tier, dominant work is about 6930/7815 seconds for tier1/tier10, leaving about 2070/1185 seconds for preparation, builds, 64 durable seals/opens, parity, serialization, hashing and finalization. No M1 baseline, extra query parallelism or retry is assumed. Slower actual throughput can exceed the estimate; preserve partial evidence.

basis./disk_min_free_bytes/base: Retain the original 24-GiB minimum, which rounded up 24 times the 952570424-byte unchanged pair in fixture-pins.json. Review C-1 frees timing serving directories only after receipt hashes/sizes, so fresh rounds do not accumulate serving copies; keep the input fixtures and evidence. The separate post-tier100-freeze formula uses actual frozen bytes/counts and can require more free space. Neither floor is a measured peak guarantee.

Actual peak is unmeasured; no evidence is deleted.
basis./disk_min_free_bytes/vector: Integration proposal: 2 GiB free, rounding up four times the 460800000-byte F32 matrix for reference scratch, outputs and headroom. Actual fixture files and existing caches are already charged when the floor is checked.
basis./software_cleanup: Supported fixed-path cleanup, not a third-party action. The current actions/runner-images Ubuntu2404 software list confirms installed Android, .NET, Haskell and CodeQL toolsets. jlumbroso/free-disk-space README reports an older ubuntu-20.04.4 sample of 14 GiB Android and 2.7 GiB .NET reclaimed; its 31 GiB total also removes things this workflow preserves. Treat the 30 GiB planning figure as uncertain, not a current-host measurement. Sources: https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md and https://github.com/jlumbroso/free-disk-space#typical-output .
basis./base_capacity: Review C-1 checks-base estimate forwarded by the lead: required_free_bytes = 2*(8*S + 300*E + 256*N) + 1073741824. S is maximum input bytes, N maximum nodes, E maximum edges over tier1, tier10 and tier100; use fixture-pins.json for tier1/10 and the frozen generated inventory for tier100. Inputs already occupy disk and are not added again. This is an admission floor, not a measured peak guarantee. Insufficient space is blocked by capacity, never a format miss. Stage 1 revision retains the conservative 300 edge-byte capacity coefficient; payload, references, offsets and any side index are counted in measured inventory, never inferred from this floor.
